set.body:
VERIFIED-GOOD, and it is the best documentation in the package - the one place where a table and the code agree exactly.

The DESCRIPTION advertises capability-gated covariance interpretations. I tested whether the gates hold, whether they open, and whether the vignette's permissions table at evidence-pairing.Rmd:443-453 describes them accurately. All three: yes.

THE GATES CLOSE.

  connectivity(view = 'canonical')     GATED  Canonical connectivity requires an explicit
                                              regularization policy.
  connectivity(view = 'gaussian')      GATED  Gaussian-information connectivity requires
                                              explicit regularization and a Gaussian model.
  construction = 'raw_product'         GATED at the CONSTRUCTOR - only psd_variation and
                                              joint_covariance are legal, so an uncertified
                                              construction cannot be built and then asked
                                              for a covariance view. The gate is at the
                                              earliest possible point, not downstream.

THE GAUSSIAN GATE IS CONJUNCTIVE, and correctly so:

  no ridge, no model      GATED
  ridge only              GATED
  model only              GATED
  ridge AND model         OPEN -> effect_coupling_result with columns
                                  edge_id, information, units

Neither ingredient alone suffices. The result carries a units column, so the information view declares its own units rather than returning a bare number.

THE OTHER GATES OPEN CORRECTLY when their contracts are met: canonical with an explicit ridge, geometry_alignment, and correlation all return effect_coupling_result with the expected columns.

THE TABLE IS ACCURATE ROW BY ROW. evidence-pairing.Rmd:443-453 states:

  effect_coupling()               any admitted fixed query; no covariance claim
  covariance_coupling()           repeated variation, effective rank above one, coherent
                                  joint covariance, valid self-blocks
  connectivity(correlation)       the covariance contract plus rank-one oriented axes
  canonical_coupling()            the covariance contract plus explicit regularization
  geometry_alignment()            coherent joint covariance and nonzero self-geometries
  Gaussian information            canonical contract plus an explicit joint Gaussian model
                                  and information units
  reconstruct_evidence()          complete edge frame, matching bases, preflight, rank

Every row I tested matches the enforced behaviour precisely, including the conjunctive Gaussian requirement and the information units.

WHY THIS BEAD MATTERS BEYOND BEING A PASS. It is the counter-example to the thesis I have been building all day. Across twelve sweeps I have argued that the documentation systematically undersells the package - four verified capabilities shown nowhere, one documented capability with no exported consumer, output that never explains itself. This table is the opposite: a piece of documentation that is precise, complete, checkable, and correct, describing the single most subtle mechanism in the package.

The vignette reviewer independently singled it out, calling it real content in a document they were otherwise harsh about.

SO THE RECOMMENDATION IS TO COPY IT, not to fix it. The permissions table is the template the rest of the documentation needs:
  it names each user-facing operation
  it states the precondition in terms of what the DATA must support, not what the framework calls it
  it is verifiable, and I verified it
  it fits in thirteen lines

If the four undersold capabilities on bd-01KZYHGE7SAN8CB8YV4BFJ1CXQ, bd-01KZYR0Y29S6G7FVY2VP61QZFW, bd-01KZYRM97WDJ6T3GDG3ATX7Y59 and bd-01KZYBK55CR0T97SE36G9ESPNP were given one table of this shape, most of the discoverability problem in this review would close.
set.title: Verified: the capability gates enforce the permissions table exactly, and that table is the template the rest of the docs need
